summary: Intermittent dedicated-pool throughput sag linked to noisy adjacent tenant + autoscaler cooldown hysteresis ("thrum")
summary_long: Customer reports periodic ~20-40% drop in steady-state throughput (p50 unchanged, p95/p99 increase) on their dedicated pool over 48h window. Drops coincide with a high number of short-lived connections from a single tenant in the same physical cluster. Hypothesis: adjacent-tenant microbursts trigger NVLink/PCIe contention and the autoscaler cooldown prevents immediate prewarm, producing a rhythmic throughput depression we are calling 'thrum'.
description:
Issue summary:
- BlueCrest reports repeating ~30% throughput degradation for their dedicated capacity during midday traffic windows across us-east. P50 of calls unchanged; P95/P99 token generation latency and observed completed inference/sec drop. No application-level errors; no 5xx rate from API.
Impact:
- Customer experiencing degraded throughput and sporadic increases in tail latency that impact SLA for sync generation routes. Affects production model gpt-3.8-open-quantized on dedicated pool.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east, single shard of reserved GPUs (A100 80GB equivalent) running serving-runtime 1.14.2, allocator v2.7, autoscaler v3.1.
Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Normal steady traffic from customer + other tenants.
2) A different tenant begins bursty short-lived streams (hundreds of 1-3s connections) across same reserved shard.
3) Within 30-90s the reserved pool shows elevated PCIe completion queue wait, NVLink error counters tick, and kernel-side GPU IO waits spike (see metrics).
4) Throughput (inferences/sec) for BlueCrest drops ~20-40% for a 2-8 minute window, then partially recovers. Pattern repeats with tenant microbursts and aligns with autoscaler backoff/cooldown windows.
Logs/metrics attached:
- Dashboard links (internal): https://dashboards.internal.redwood.ai/d/DEDICATED/throughput-sag?orgId=1&var-pool=bluecrest-us-east
- Sample allocator traces: allocator.log:2026-03-11T13:14:22Z ALLOC_ATTEMPT tenantId=tc-334 path=/v2/generate cpuWait=0.02 gpuWait=0.48
- NVLink counters: nvlink_errs: {timestamp:2026-03-11T13:14:30Z, counter_delta:24}
- Sidecar logs show concurrent health-scan workers ramping from 2->18 during microbursts (sidecar.log).
steps_taken: 1) Confirmed correlation between tenant short-session rate and throughput sag via connection telemetry. 2) Scoped issue to same physical reserved shard using allocation traces and nvlink counters. 3) Temporarily rate-limited the noisy tenant's short-lived connection burst at the edge to reduce microburst amplitude. 4) Increased dedicated pool prewarm target by +10% for the customer as a temporary buffer. 5) Adjusted autoscaler cooldown from 120s->60s in the affected region to make it more responsive while we investigate. 6) Gathered additional traces and NVLink kernel metrics; reproduced locally in a staging cluster with synthetic short-connection generator.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and hypotheses:
- 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC: Customer reported first sustained pattern.
- 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC: Observed microburst tenant that opens ~800 short-lived streams/minute across shard.
- Hypothesis A (noisy neighbor IO): Frequent short streams cause GPU driver/page-table churn and NVLink/PCIe saturation leading to observed GPU IO wait. Evidence: NVLink error counter spikes coincide with throughput sag.
- Hypothesis B (autoscaler hysteresis): Autoscaler uses a smoothing window that delays prewarm when load is highly spiky; combined with (A) we get under-provisioning for 2-8 minutes. Evidence: autoscaler metric window shows undershoot during spike->cooldown sequence.
- Hypothesis C (sidecar health-scan amplification): Sidecar health scan concurrency increases during microbursts, generating background NVMe/io traffic that competes with inference GPU DMA. Evidence: sidecar logs show worker ramp-ups aligned to microbursts.
Partial findings:
- Reproduced behaviour in staging by replaying short-connection pattern, measured PCIe completion queue saturation and increased kernel-level gpu-sleep times.
- Allocation traces show tenant prefetches and short-lived sessions causing more frequent kernel context switches.
- No driver crashes, no OOMs. Thermal telemetry normal.
Next steps:
- Run controlled A/B where we throttle sidecar health-scan in staging to observe delta.
- Work with infra team to add fine-grained NVLink and PCIe counters to the dedicated pool dashboard.
- Prepare a fix to sampling behavior in autoscaler smoothing algorithm (reduce smoothing weight on very short-lived-connection signals).
comments: 2026-03-10 | Asha Patel (Support): Initial report from BlueCrest. Collected traces and requested permission to update autoscaler settings temporarily.

2026-03-11 | Luis Romero (SRE): Scoped to reserved shard id rs-42; reproduced microburst locally. Ordered temporary edge rate-limit on noisy tenant to 150 rps (was 800 rps). Observed recovery of BlueCrest throughput to ~90% baseline.

2026-03-11 | Maria Chen (Platform Eng): Noted sidecar version 2.3.1 has health-scan concurrency regression. Filing PR to cap concurrency. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/587

2026-03-11 | Luis Romero (SRE): Adjusted autoscaler cooldown for rs-42 from 120s->60s as stopgap. Autoscaler responded faster on subsequent microbursts; p99 still elevated. Need allocator fairness fix.
2026-03-12 | Asha Patel (Support): Customer acknowledges improved behavior after temporary measures but requests root cause and durable fix before next month. Asked for timeline and post-mortem.
2026-03-12 | Product Ops: Requesting prioritized work item to modify allocator heuristics to consider short-connection churn and NVLink counters.
resolution: Temporary mitigations applied: edge rate-limit for noisy tenant, increased prewarm buffer for BlueCrest, reduced autoscaler cooldown in region. Sidecar concurrency cap PR merged to staging (see related PR). Long-term fixes planned: allocator fairness patch (PR in progress), autoscaler smoothing refactor to weight short-lived-connection signals, and enhanced cluster NVLink/PCIe telemetry. Customer notified of mitigations and next steps.
resolution_notes: Workarounds in place as of 2026-03-11 16:40 UTC. No customer-facing downtime. Follow-ups: 1) Allocator PR #1198 targeted for 2026-03-18 deploy to canary. 2) Autoscaler smoothing change scheduled for 2026-03-20. 3) Add NVLink counters to dedicated-pool dashboard by 2026-03-17. 4) Postmortem doc due 2026-03-22 and share with BlueCrest.

outage_impact: No total outage. Degraded throughput and elevated tail latency for customer routes during microburst windows. SLA impact minimal after mitigations but customer requests durable fixes.
notes_for_engineering: Repro playbook in staging: run short-connection generator (see scripts/short_fanout_generator) at 600-900 rps across shard, collect nvlink,pci,allocator traces. Instrument autoscaler smoothing inputs and compare with baseline. Consider gating sidecar background scans when GPU IO wait > threshold.
customer_communication: 2026-03-11: Informed BlueCrest of temporary rate limit and autoscaler cooldown change; customer observed significant improvement. 2026-03-12: Confirmed customer satisfied with temporary mitigations and awaiting permanent fixes. Postmortem to be shared.
priority_rationale: P1 due to production degradation for a paying dedicated customer, repeated pattern affecting throughput and tail latency; requires SRE/Platform work across teams.
estimated_time_to_fix: 2 weeks for full allocator+autoscaler changes; interim mitigations already applied
acceptance_criteria: 1) No recurring throughput sag >10% during synthetic microbursts in staging. 2) NVLink/PCIe counters do not show repeated saturation under the same short-stream load after allocator+autoscaler patches. 3) BlueCrest confirms stable throughput for 72h in prod post-deploy.
customer_notes: BlueCrest engineering: 'We see immediate improvement after your temporary throttling and autoscaler tweak. We'll hold off heavy midday experiments until you confirm fixes.'
